description: Fig. 8 is a composite two-part benchmark grid (mixed modality: raw micrographs plus colour-coded segmentation output maps) comparing MatSAM against SAM on noisy micrographs. Both (a) and (b) are 3-row x 5-column layouts with row labels 'Noisy image', 'MatSAM' and 'SAM' and columns labelled Var.=0.00, 0.01, 0.05, 0.10 and 0.20 for salt-and-pepper noise. (a) uses a 'DP590-2 (SEM)' micrograph of dual-phase steel, showing light elongated/globular grains in a darker matrix that becomes visibly speckled towards higher variance; its MatSAM row is annotated IoU 0.822, 0.735, 0.601, 0.554, 0.549 and its SAM row IoU 0.768, 0.636, 0.577, 0.449, 0.485. (b) uses an 'AZA (XCT)' X-ray tomography slice of AlZn alloy with darker globular features; MatSAM row IoU 0.946, 0.913, 0.879, 0.861, 0.815 and SAM row IoU 0.903, 0.884, 0.814, 0.819, 0.776. Segmentation masks are white phase on black, with pink and blue pixels marking under- and over-segmentation errors. MatSAM's printed IoU is higher than SAM's at every noise level in both datasets, and declines more gracefully as variance rises, demonstrating greater noise robustness of the training-free MatSAM pipeline.

subfigures.description: 3x5 grid on an SEM micrograph of dual-phase steel 'DP590-2 (SEM)'. Top row: noisy greyscale image at Var.=0.00, 0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, showing progressive salt-and-pepper speckle. Middle row 'MatSAM': white-on-black segmentation masks annotated IoU 0.822, 0.735, 0.601, 0.554, 0.549. Bottom row 'SAM': masks annotated IoU 0.768, 0.636, 0.577, 0.449, 0.485. Pink/blue overlay pixels mark under-/over-segmentation.

3x5 grid on an XCT slice of AlZn alloy 'AZA (XCT)' with darker globular features on grey matrix. Top row: noisy image at the same five Var. levels. Middle row 'MatSAM': masks annotated IoU 0.946, 0.913, 0.879, 0.861, 0.815. Bottom row 'SAM': masks annotated IoU 0.903, 0.884, 0.814, 0.819, 0.776. Error overlays (pink under-segmentation, blue over-segmentation) grow with noise, earlier and larger for SAM.

observations.observation: Fig. 8 is a two-part composite grid; each part (a) and (b) carries three row labels ('Noisy image', 'MatSAM', 'SAM') and five columns labelled Var.=0.00, 0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20.

Panel (a) top row is labelled 'DP590-2 (SEM)' and shows a dual-phase steel SEM micrograph of light elongated/globular grains on a darker matrix, with salt-and-pepper speckle visibly increasing from left to right.
Panel (b) top row is labelled 'AZA (XCT)' and shows a grey X-ray computed tomography slice of an AlZn alloy containing darker globular features on a lighter matrix.
In (a) the MatSAM row prints IoU values 0.822, 0.735, 0.601, 0.554 and 0.549 for Var.=0.00, 0.01, 0.05, 0.10 and 0.20 respectively.
In (a) the SAM row prints IoU values 0.768, 0.636, 0.577, 0.449 and 0.485 across the same noise series.
In (b) the MatSAM row prints IoU values 0.946, 0.913, 0.879, 0.861 and 0.815, and the SAM row prints 0.903, 0.884, 0.814, 0.819 and 0.776.
MatSAM's printed IoU is higher than SAM's at every one of the five noise levels in both the SEM (DP590-2) and XCT (AZA) panels.

MatSAM's IoU decreases monotonically with increasing noise variance in both panels, whereas SAM in (a) falls from 0.768 to 0.449 between Var.=0.00 and Var.=0.10 and then partially recovers to 0.485 at Var.=0.20, and SAM in (b) rises slightly from 0.814 to 0.819 between Var.=0.05 and Var.=0.10.
The segmentation masks are white segmented phase on a black background, with small magenta/pink and cyan/blue overlay pixels marking segmentation errors concentrated on the smaller grains.
The caption states that pink and blue regions represent under- and over-segmentation, respectively.
The caption states that (a) shows results on an SEM image from the dual-phase steel dataset DP590-2 and (b) on an XCT image from the AlZn alloy dataset AzA.

The citing text states the comparison was performed against the original SAM method on representative SEM (DP590-2) and XCT (AZA) images, with salt-and-pepper (S&P) noise introduced via the scikit-image random noise generation function and noise levels adjusted by variance Var. = 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2.
The citing text states that speckle and Gaussian noise were tested in the same experiment and are reported in Supplementary Note 1, so Fig. 8 covers only the salt-and-pepper case.

unreadable_items: individual error pixels (pink/blue) in the mask rows cannot be attributed to specific grains at the supplied resolution
